summary: The note surveys startups applying blockchain beyond cryptocurrency, covering supply chain, real estate, legal, sharing economy, voting, carbon tracking, health records, IoT, finance, education, media and data storage. It gives each startup's focus and launch timing, and argues blockchain brings transparency, efficiency and security to many industries.
one_line: Overview of blockchain startups across supply chain, voting, health, education, media and more, showing uses beyond cryptocurrency.
key_facts: Blockchain came into the spotlight after the creation of Bitcoin in 2009 and was initially seen as a mere ledger for cryptocurrency transactions.
Alice Johnson and her team at ChainSecure unveiled a platform integrating blockchain into supply chain management, with the narrative shifting around late 2023.
In its October 2023 milestone release, ChainSecure reported a 75% decrease in the time taken to identify and respond to supply chain disruptions.

On November 15, 2023, Robert Tan, CEO of SmartContracts Inc., spoke at the Blockchain Innovators Conference about the need for trustless systems; his company uses smart contracts in real estate for automatic property transfers.
LegalChain uses blockchain to authenticate legal documents, preventing fraud and reducing verification time.
ShareBlock, which entered the market in September 2023, built a decentralized platform for sharing goods and services with transactions recorded on a transparent ledger.
On December 3, 2023, VoteLedger was featured on the cover of Tech Democracy for its secure voting platform that encrypts and tallies votes without tampering risk.
EcoChain, founded in January 2024, monitors a company's emissions in real time and offsets them by buying carbon credits or investing in green initiatives.
MedBlock, launched in February 2024, creates a unified, tamper-proof repository of health records for doctors and providers.
SecureThings introduced a platform to secure IoT devices in April 2024 by decentralizing the network through which devices communicate.
BorderlessBank is cited for cross-border trades and international transactions.
EdChain, which emerged in summer 2024, records academic credentials on the blockchain to streamline verification for employers and institutions.
CreatorChain, founded in the third quarter of 2024, lets content creators keep control of their intellectual property and engage directly with audiences.
DecentralizeData gained investor interest after its pitch at the TechCrunch Disrupt event of 2024 and offers decentralized data storage that removes the single point of failure.
